samples.summary: Phase 25's design doc still records the behaviour this change deleted: "Local review is a convenience, not authority: `spec-to-pr.mjs review` … needs `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and degrades to a warn-and-skip when it is absent. The authoritative panel is still the cloud one." The diff removes the token requirement and the skip (`ambientAuthNotice`), and `docs/design/agentic-dev-loop.md` §1.1 now states the opposite — that for an ordinary branch the local round is the only machine review. The repo's discipline is to fold a change into the canonical subsystem doc rather than leave a second, contradicting statement elsewhere; harness-engineering.md is where the phase is recorded and it was not updated. Cost stays inside the docs (the code works as specified), but a reader following the harness doc will believe local review can be skipped for free.
samples.evidence: docs/design/harness-engineering.md:2403-2406 ("needs CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and degrades to a warn-and-skip") vs scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs `ambientAuthNotice` + docs/design/agentic-dev-loop.md:83 ("it is the only machine review the change gets")

samples.summary: The loop's policy — max 3 rounds, the per-round lens rotation, the rebuttal rule, the "get a human past round 3" rule — is now written out in full in four places: `.claude/commands/self-review.md`, `CLAUDE.md` step 3, `CONTRIBUTING.md` step 3 and `docs/design/agentic-dev-loop.md` §1.1, and the bound is also a constant (`MAX_SELF_REVIEW_ROUNDS`) enforced in `spec-to-pr.mjs`. Nothing links the copies (no test or doc-ref guard as with `PAGED_LATCH`/the panel drift guard), so changing the bound or the rotation means editing five sites and the four prose copies will diverge. The repo's own convention for a rule duplicated outside a module is to state it once canonically and reference it; the two contributor-facing files could point at `/self-review` and the design doc instead of restating the mechanics.

Layering: `spec-to-pr.mjs` is documented as the agent-track local front door (branch → implement → handoff), and this change grows it by ~600 lines of a general-purpose local review-loop store (round directories, temp-dir safety guards, branch keying, terminal sanitisation, panel spawn seam) for a subcommand the new header itself says is "NOT AGENT-TRACK-ONLY, despite this file's name". That admission is the signal the new machinery belongs in its own module (e.g. `self-review-rounds.mjs`) that both `/self-review` and `spec-to-pr handoff` consume, matching how the rest of scripts/agent factors shared mechanics (`rounds.mjs`, `prior-findings.mjs`, `review-state.mjs`). No behavioural consequence, so the cost is confined to the file's growing scope.
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:20-27 header comment; the file grows from ~350 to ~1130 lines with the round store, `unsafeBaseReason`, `ownedPathChain`, `branchKey`, `printable`, `panelScript`

samples.summary: §1.1 says the local loop "carries each round's still-gating findings into the next (`carryForwardFindings`, shared with the cloud's projection)", but the cloud path does not call `carryForwardFindings` — `agent-review-panel.yml` keeps its own inline github-script copy, and only the two selection filters are pinned by the new drift-guard test (the projected field lists already differ: local carries `line` and raw `severity`, the workflow normalises `severity` and reshapes `mergedFrom`). "Shared" overstates the coupling; "mirrors, guarded by inspection" is what is actually true.
